leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice President (previously Provost)
leaders.nextRole: President
leaders.notes: Championed SJSU as the metropolitan university of Silicon Valley. After Towson he led the University of Massachusetts System (2011-2015) and then became Chancellor of the University System of Maryland (2015-2020). Anchor president in office in 1996.

leaders.priorTitle: President Emeritus and Regents Professor (retired president)
leaders.nextRole: President Emeritus/Regents Professor (later UNR interim president 2005-2006)
leaders.notes: The longest-serving president of the University of Nevada, Reno (1978-2001); came out of retirement to serve one academic year as SJSU interim president during 2003-2004. Died in 2017.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.priorInstitution: State University of New York College at Brockport (SUNY Brockport)
leaders.nextRole: Returned to a position with SUNY (his former employer)
leaders.notes: Named president April 20, 2004, effective July 15; resigned August 1, 2004 after about three weeks, citing health reasons, and returned to New York. One of the shortest presidential tenures in SJSU history.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Administration and Finance / CFO (also SJSU interim president Aug 2004-Apr 2005 immediately before)
leaders.nextRole: Retired; President Emeritus (returned as interim president in 2010)
leaders.notes: Served as SJSU VP for Administration and Finance/CFO from 1993-2004, then interim president (Aug 2004-Apr 2005) before being named permanent president (May 2005-June 2008). Earlier administrative roles at Murray State University and Western State College of Colorado.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.nextRole: Chief Executive Officer
leaders.notes: President of Texas Tech University for five years before SJSU; earlier provost at the University of Iowa (1996-2003). Led ACT, Inc. as CEO from 2010 to 2015.

leaders.priorTitle: President Emeritus (retired former SJSU president, called back from retirement)
leaders.nextRole: Returned to retirement as President Emeritus
leaders.notes: Returned from retirement to serve a second interim presidency (Aug 2010-July 2011) bridging the departure of Jon Whitmore and the arrival of Mohammad Qayoumi.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.nextRole: Chief Advisor for Infrastructure and Technology to the President of Afghanistan (Ashraf Ghani); later acting Minister of Finance
leaders.notes: Born in Afghanistan; first person of Afghan descent to head a major U.S. university. President of Cal State East Bay (2006-2011) and earlier CFO at CSU Northridge; had also been SJSU's VP for administration 1986-1995. Left SJSU in 2015 to advise President Ghani.

leaders.priorTitle: President (President Emerita after stepping down July 2015)
leaders.nextRole: Retired (returned to Michigan as President Emerita)
leaders.notes: President of Eastern Michigan University (2008-2015), that university's first female president. Appointed SJSU interim president August 18, 2015, eleven days after stepping down from EMU; served through July 1, 2016.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.nextRole: Interim CEO, Business-Higher Education Forum; then Executive Vice President, Association of Governing Boards (AGB)
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: Business-Higher Education Forum / Association of Governing Boards of Universities and Colleges
leaders.notes: SJSU's 30th president; before SCSU (2012-2016) she was provost at Lehman College, CUNY. Resigned effective December 21, 2021 amid fallout from the Scott Shaw sports-medicine sexual-misconduct case and a Title IX cover-up investigation involving the athletics program.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs (and professor of economics)
leaders.nextRole: President
leaders.notes: Appointed by CSU Chancellor Joseph Castro; assumed SJSU interim leadership January 3, 2022 after Papazian's resignation and served until Teniente-Matson took office January 2023. Named president of CSU Chico effective July 1, 2023.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.notes: SJSU's 31st president and its first Latina president; took office January 2023. Led Texas A&M-San Antonio (2015-2023) and earlier was VP for Administration/CFO at CSU Fresno (2004-2015). Sitting president as of July 2026; no active presidential search.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Student Affairs
leaders.priorInstitution: South Carolina State University (internal; longtime SC State administrator, previously Director of Institutional Self-Studies and Vice Provost for Academic Administration)
leaders.nextRole: Retired (president emeritus)
leaders.notes: 8th president. Named interim president June 13, 1995, then permanent president April 10, 1996; served to 2002. SC State alumnus (B.S. 1971) with a Ph.D. in molecular biology from Purdue. Anchor president in office in 1996.

leaders.priorTitle: Retired Chief Justice of the South Carolina Supreme Court
leaders.priorInstitution: Supreme Court of South Carolina (retired from the court in 2000)
leaders.nextRole: Returned to private life; practiced and taught law
leaders.notes: Named interim president July 1, 2002. First African American Chief Justice of the SC Supreme Court in the modern era. Died December 3, 2017.

leaders.priorTitle: Interim Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer
leaders.priorInstitution: South Carolina State University (internal; a 30-year SC State administrator and mathematics professor)
leaders.nextRole: President (11th)
leaders.notes: 9th president. Board declined to renew his contract in December 2007; he departed in 2008. Ph.D. from Michigan State; two SC State degrees.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean, College of Education, Humanities and Social Sciences
leaders.nextRole: Returned to SC State faculty/administration
leaders.notes: Named interim president December 13, 2007, after the board did not renew Hugine's contract; served until Cooper was hired in July 2008.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior program administrator (17 years) with the National Institute of Food and Agriculture
leaders.priorInstitution: U.S. Department of Agriculture (Washington, DC); earlier faculty/administrative roles at Alabama A&M and Tuskegee
leaders.nextRole: Senior Fellow (AASCU), then Executive Director of the White House Initiative on HBCUs
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: American Association of State Colleges and Universities, then the U.S. Department of Education / White House Initiative on HBCUs
leaders.notes: 10th president; named June 2008. Ph.D. in animal nutrition (University of Illinois). Left amid a board investigation in 2012. Died July 2015; President Obama issued a statement on his passing.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior administrator (later Executive Director of Institutional Effectiveness)
leaders.nextRole: Returned to SC State administration (Executive Director of Institutional Effectiveness)
leaders.notes: Assumed responsibilities as acting president March 31, 2012, in the gap after Cooper's departure; served until Warrick's interim appointment took effect July 5, 2012. Exact pre-acting VP title not fully confirmable in sources reviewed.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Fellow, School of Pharmacy (Center for Minority Health Services Research)
leaders.nextRole: Interim President
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: Grambling State University (2014); later President of Stillman College (2017) and Prairie View A&M University (2023)
leaders.notes: Became interim president July 5, 2012. A pharmacist and environmental-health scientist; later the first female president of Stillman College and subsequently president of Prairie View A&M.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.priorInstitution: South Carolina State University (internal; joined SC State August 2012)
leaders.nextRole: Returned to his provost/VP for Academic Affairs role (then a second interim presidency 2015-2016)
leaders.notes: Served as acting president briefly in 2013, bridging Warrick's departure and Elzey's arrival. First of two stints leading the institution.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice President for Finance, Administration and Operations
leaders.nextRole: Departed higher-ed leadership (no subsequent presidency identified)
leaders.notes: 11th president; named April 18, 2013, assumed office June 15, 2013. Placed on administrative leave by the board in February 2015 amid a severe budget/enrollment crisis and departed that year.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.nextRole: President (9th)
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: Voorhees College (August 2016); later President of West Liberty University, WV (January 2021)
leaders.notes: Second stint leading SC State, as interim/acting president from 2015 into 2016 after Elzey; credited with a balanced budget and enrollment recovery. Stepped down about a month before being named Voorhees president.

leaders.priorTitle: Retired corporate executive; member of the SC State Board of Trustees immediately prior
leaders.priorInstitution: South Carolina State University Board of Trustees (career included VP of AT&T's computer division and executive roles at Exxon, General Electric and Gillette; MIT / MIT Sloan graduate)
leaders.nextRole: Retired (subsequently litigated his dismissal; suit later settled)
leaders.notes: 12th president; began July 1, 2016. Fired by a 10-3 board vote on July 13, 2021, initially 'for cause,' later reclassified 'without cause'; enrollment decline was widely cited.

leaders.priorTitle: Acting/Interim President of SC State (July 2021-April 2022); immediately before that, Vice President for Strategic Alliances and Initiatives
leaders.priorInstitution: South Carolina State University (internal; joined May 2021). Before returning to SC State he was Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Army Review Boards (federal Senior Executive Service) after a 28+ year U.S. Army career.
leaders.notes: 13th president. Retired U.S. Army colonel and SC State alumnus. Named acting president July 13, 2021, interim August 25, 2021, and permanent president April 28, 2022. Enrollment rose ~32% under his leadership; the board extended his contract through 2031, so there is no active presidential search.

leaders.priorTitle: Longtime SDSU administrator (rural sociologist and academic vice president)
leaders.nextRole: Retired
leaders.notes: 17th president, serving 1985 to 1997. Announced on January 9, 1997 that he would retire effective January 1, 1998; the Board of Regents named his successor in October 1997. Anchor president in office in 1996.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Fellow and Acting Vice President for Academic and International Programs
leaders.priorInstitution: American Association of State Colleges and Universities (AASCU), Washington, D.C.
leaders.nextRole: Retired; President and Professor of Education Emeritus
leaders.notes: 18th president and the first woman to lead SDSU, taking office January 1, 1998, the same day Wagner's retirement took effect. Announced retirement in December 2005 and stepped down at the end of 2006; inducted into the South Dakota Hall of Fame in 2024.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Technology and Economic Development (system office); previously dean of the College of Agricultural, Consumer and Environmental Sciences
leaders.priorInstitution: University of Illinois System / University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign
leaders.nextRole: Interim Dean, College of Business (2017-2018); corporate board director (Monsanto, Raven Industries)
leaders.notes: 19th president, an SDSU alumnus (B.S. 1969) who spent about 30 years at the University of Illinois as professor, department head, dean and system vice president before returning to lead SDSU from January 2007 to 2016.

leaders.priorTitle: South Dakota Corn Utilization Council Endowed Dean of the College of Agriculture and Biological Sciences
leaders.priorInstitution: South Dakota State University (the dean role was at SDSU itself); earlier Executive Director of the King Ranch Institute for Ranch Management at Texas A&M University-Kingsville
leaders.notes: 20th president, an SDSU alumnus who assumed office May 23, 2016 and is widely cited as the first enrolled member of a federally recognized tribe (Rosebud Sioux) to lead an 1862 land-grant university. Remains president in 2026 (outlining 2026 priorities in February 2026); no retirement announcement or active presidential search reported.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior administrator (rose through the ranks at SCSU)
leaders.nextRole: Retired
leaders.notes: First graduate of Southern to become its president; served 19 years and the campus student center is named for him. Retired in 2003 and died July 31, 2005 (age 65) in an automobile crash while on an anniversary trip in Italy. Anchor president in office in 1996.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.nextRole: Returned to Provost / Vice President for Academic Affairs role
leaders.notes: Longtime SCSU faculty member who joined as a mathematics professor in 1965 (a ~47-year tenure at Southern). Served as interim president between Adanti's 2003 retirement and Norton's 2004 arrival.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.priorInstitution: Metropolitan State College of Denver (now Metropolitan State University of Denver), where she spent ~28 years
leaders.nextRole: President
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: Slippery Rock University of Pennsylvania (2012; its first female president)
leaders.notes: SCSU's 10th president and first female president. Departure was contentious: effectively dismissed by the CSU system (announced publicly Feb 2010, tenure ending end of May 2010) under a confidential separation agreement. Later became president of Slippery Rock University.

leaders.priorTitle: Chancellor (2007-2009); earlier President of Coppin State University (2003-2007)
leaders.nextRole: Returned to academia (subsequent post not verified)
leaders.notes: Served as interim president May 3, 2010 to December 8, 2011. Sources citing 'April 2011' refer to a later re-affirmation/permanent-search episode; he withdrew his name from consideration for the permanent presidency. Most recent major executive role before SCSU was Chancellor of NC A&T (resigned 2009).

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Senior Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.priorInstitution: Lehman College, City University of New York (CUNY)
leaders.nextRole: President (30th)
leaders.notes: SCSU's 11th president; appointment approved Dec 8, 2011, took office February 1, 2012. Left in 2016 to become president of San Jose State University. Earlier dean at Montclair State University and began her career at Oakland University.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.priorInstitution: Lyndon State College, Vermont (2012-2016; later part of Northern Vermont University). Earlier VP for Enrollment Management and Student Affairs at Queens College/CUNY.
leaders.nextRole: President
leaders.notes: SCSU's 12th president; first day Aug 22, 2016. Openly gay and publicly out throughout his tenure. Announced departure March 3, 2023, concluding June 30/July 1, 2023, to become president of Stockton University.

leaders.priorTitle: Campus CEO
leaders.priorInstitution: Housatonic Community College, Bridgeport CT (since 2020; earlier interim president of Harris-Stowe State University and 13 years its provost)
leaders.nextRole: Executive Director of Systemwide Advancement
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: CSCU (Connecticut State Colleges and Universities) system office
leaders.notes: Named interim president March 31, 2023; began June 1, 2023 and served through June 30, 2025. A permanent presidential search launched under him concluded in late 2024 without a hire. Transitioned to a CSCU system-office advancement role.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean of the College of Health and Human Services
leaders.priorInstitution: Southern Connecticut State University (internal; ~26 years at Southern, previously professor of public health)
leaders.notes: Current (as of 2026) interim president; appointed by Chancellor Terrence Cheng, began July 1, 2025. ACTIVE SEARCH: the prior permanent presidential search concluded in late 2024 without a hire; a new SCSU presidential search is slated to launch in Fall 2026, after a system-wide CSCU leadership search. Longtime internal leader.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice Chancellor for Student Affairs
leaders.priorInstitution: Southern University and A&M College (internal; SU alumnus who worked at Southern from 1962, including as professor of education and dean of the Junior Division)
leaders.nextRole: Resigned (returned to private life)
leaders.notes: Chancellor of the Baton Rouge campus 1991-1998; resigned in December 1997 amid a scholarship controversy. Anchor chancellor in office in 1996. Died in 2018.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost (appointed interim chancellor December 1997 after Yates resigned, then named permanent chancellor)
leaders.nextRole: Stepped down; not verified beyond retirement from the chancellorship
leaders.notes: Served as Baton Rouge campus chancellor from 1998 (interim from December 1997) until stepping down around 2007-2008 ahead of Lomotey's July 2008 arrival.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice President and Provost
leaders.nextRole: Senior Fellow at AASCU (2012-2013), then Bardo Distinguished Professor of Educational Leadership at Western Carolina University (2013-)
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: American Association of State Colleges and Universities / Western Carolina University
leaders.notes: Took office July 1, 2008. Resigned under pressure in November 2010 but the board asked him to remain through June 2011; James Llorens succeeded him July 1, 2011. Earlier president of Fort Valley State University.

leaders.priorTitle: Professor of Public Administration and former Dean of the Graduate School
leaders.priorInstitution: Southern University and A&M College (internal; a longtime SU faculty member and administrator, also chair of political science)
leaders.nextRole: Retired; later held Baton Rouge city-parish government administrative roles
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: City of Baton Rouge / East Baton Rouge Parish government
leaders.notes: Named chancellor April 2011, took office July 1, 2011; served to 2014. A native of Alexandria, LA. Died in April 2026.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice Chancellor for Finance and Administration
leaders.nextRole: Returned to Vice Chancellor for Finance and Administration role
leaders.notes: A CPA and 43-year Southern University administrator; named acting chancellor effective July 1, 2014, serving until Ray Belton took the combined role in 2015.

leaders.priorTitle: Chancellor of Southern University at Shreveport (SUSLA), 2000-2015
leaders.nextRole: Retired (President-Chancellor Emeritus)
leaders.notes: First person to hold the combined role of Southern University System President and SUBR Chancellor after the board consolidated the two positions in March 2015. Retired effective fall 2022 after seven years.

leaders.priorTitle: Chancellor of the University of Wisconsin-Platteville (2010-2022)
leaders.nextRole: Continued as Southern University System President after the SUBR Chancellor role was separated from the system presidency
leaders.notes: Named February 2022 as Southern University System President and SUBR Chancellor (combined President-Chancellor). In 2024 the board re-separated the Baton Rouge campus chancellorship, which went to John K. Pierre while Shields continued as System President.

leaders.priorTitle: Chancellor of the Southern University Law Center (2016-2024); also SU System interim executive vice president
leaders.notes: Named chancellor March 22, 2024, took office July 2024, and formally invested March 2026; his appointment re-established the Baton Rouge campus chancellorship as a position separate from the system presidency. Longtime SU Law Center faculty member (since 1990).
